newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian sugar terminals at 100 mln/t mark.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian sugar terminals at 100 mln/t mark.

text.p: The 100 millionth tonne of bulk handled Australian raws would be received at one of Queensland's seven sugar terminals this week, marking a major milestone, Queensland Sugar Corp (QSC) chief executive David Rutledge said.

This would represent nearly 40 years of progressive development since the first tonne of raw sugar using mechanised bulk handling technology was received in 1957 with the opening of the Mackay Bulk Sugar Terminal, he said in a statement.
Rutledge said infrastructure gave the Queensland sugar industry a significant edge against its competitors.
Queensland was the world leader in bulk handling of raw sugar with the largest, most advanced bulk storage and handling facilities in the world, he said.
Loading a 30,000 tonne ship with bagged sugar used to take up to six weeks, but now could be achieved in 24 hours, he said.
Seven bulk terminals in Queensland were built between 1957 and 1985 and had been continually upgraded.
This year a record five million tonnes of raw sugar would be received at the terminals and this had already resulted in record shipments in July of 790,000 tonnes, he said.
In the past 40 years, more than 750 million tonnes of sugar cane had been crushed to produce 100 million tonnes of raws.
Based on Australia's current annual consumption, this would supply the Australian population for about 100 years, he said.
QSC is the owner of almost all of Australia's sugar crop.
